name: s390_runtime_instr
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_s390_runtime_instr, int command, int signum);
description: The s390_runtime_instr() system call starts or stops CPU run-time instrumentation for the calling thread. The command argument specifies whether to start or stop instrumentation, while the signum argument is ignored in current kernels.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Controls whether to start (S390_RUNTIME_INSTR_START, 1) or stop (S390_RUNTIME_INSTR_STOP, 2) run-time instrumentation for the calling thread.

parameters.name: signum
parameters.description: Specifies a real-time signal number, which was intended for delivering signals on certain events but is ignored in kernels from Linux 4.4 onwards.

return_value.success: Returns 0 on success, enabling the thread for run-time instrumentation.
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error.

errors.description: The value specified in command is not a valid command.
The value specified in signum is not a real-time signal number (though this does not cause an error in kernels from Linux 4.4 onwards).
Allocating memory for the run-time instrumentation control block failed.
The run-time instrumentation facility is not available.
